Name: Theme Sort
Purpose: Group similar ideas, observations or pieces of information into meaningful themes to reveal patterns and support discussion.
Inputs: Assumptions, Ideas, Insights, Opportunities, Research, Stakeholders, User feedback
Outcomes: Alignment, Opportunity discovery, Problem clarity, Shared understanding
Preparation Needed:
Prepare a board or workspace where notes can be moved freely.

Ensure participants have already generated or collected information to sort.

Theme Sort works best after idea generation, research review or information gathering activities.
Facilitator Notes:
Encourage participants to move notes silently before discussing.

Focus on identifying natural patterns rather than forcing categories.

Avoid naming themes too early.

When clusters begin to emerge, ask participants what connects the items.

Once clusters stabilise, create clear labels that describe the theme.

The goal is not organisation for its own sake. The goal is shared understanding.

Name: Blind Vote
Purpose: Allow participants to make independent decisions without being influenced by dominant voices, hierarchy or groupthink.
Inputs: Assumptions, Decision needed, Ideas, Objective, Opportunities, Problem statement, Risks
Preparation Needed:
Clearly define what is being voted on.

Ensure all options are visible and understood by participants.

Decide voting criteria before starting.

Prepare a method for collecting votes simultaneously.
Facilitator Notes:
Do not allow participants to discuss their choices before voting.

Ensure everyone understands the options and criteria.

Ask participants to vote independently.

Reveal all votes at the same time.

Use discussion only after votes have been revealed.

If there is no clear outcome, run a second round or use the result to focus the next discussion.

Blind Vote is designed to reduce bias and create a more honest view of group opinion.

Name: Parking Lot
Purpose: Capture off-topic questions, risks or ideas without derailing the workshop.
Preparation Needed: Create a clearly visible Parking Lot section on the workshop board before the session begins.
Facilitator Notes:
Use the Parking Lot whenever discussions drift away from the workshop objective.

Acknowledge the contribution, capture it visibly and return focus to the current activity.

Review the Parking Lot before the workshop closes and decide whether items require actions, follow-up discussions or can be discarded.

Name: Who, What, When
Purpose: Turn decisions, ideas or recommendations into clear actions with ownership and accountability.
Preparation Needed:
Prepare a simple structure with three columns:

Who
What
When

Ensure decisions or actions have already been identified before running this technique.
Facilitator Notes:
Push for specific actions rather than vague intentions.

Every action should have a named owner and a clear deadline.

Avoid assigning actions to groups or teams.

Focus on commitment and accountability.

Name: Dot Vote
Purpose: Quickly identify group preferences by allowing participants to distribute votes across multiple options.
Preparation Needed:
Display all options clearly and ensure participants understand the voting criteria.

Decide how many votes each participant receives before starting.
Facilitator Notes:
Dot voting is best used to identify preferences, not make final decisions.

Ask participants to vote silently.

Review results as a group and discuss any surprising outcomes.

If required, use Blind Vote afterwards to make a final decision.

Name: Five Whys
Purpose: Explore the underlying causes of a problem by repeatedly asking why it is occurring.
Outcomes: Problem clarity, Root cause discovery, Shared understanding
Preparation Needed:
Start with a clearly defined problem statement.

Prepare space to capture each why and the corresponding answer.
Facilitator Notes:
Focus on understanding the system rather than assigning blame.

Do not force exactly five rounds.

Stop when the group reaches a meaningful root cause that they can influence.

If multiple causes emerge, capture them separately rather than forcing a single answer.

Purpose: Create alignment around a shared objective and define measurable indicators of success.
Preparation Needed: Create alignment around a shared objective and define measurable indicators of success.
Facilitator Notes:

Challenge vague objectives and encourage measurable key results.

Focus on outcomes rather than outputs.

Use voting when alignment cannot be reached through discussion.

Name: Problem Statement
Purpose: Create a clear and shared understanding of the problem that needs to be solved.
Preparation Needed:
Gather research, insights and evidence related to the challenge.

Ensure participants have enough context to discuss the problem before beginning.
Facilitator Notes:
Keep the group focused on the problem rather than solutions.

Challenge assumptions and vague language.

A good problem statement should be specific, evidence-based and understandable by everyone in the room.

Name: How Might We
Purpose: Reframe problems into opportunity-focused questions that encourage solution exploration.
Preparation Needed:
Prepare a clear problem statement.

Ensure participants understand the challenge before beginning.

Create space to capture multiple How Might We statements and resulting ideas.
Facilitator Notes:
Avoid writing How Might We statements that already contain a solution.

Encourage participants to generate multiple statements before discussing them.

Keep questions broad enough to inspire creativity but focused enough to remain relevant to the challenge.

Name: Impact Effort Map
Purpose: Evaluate opportunities, ideas or actions by comparing their expected impact against the effort required to deliver them.
Preparation Needed:
Prepare a matrix with two axes:

Impact
Effort

Ensure participants understand the evaluation criteria before placing items on the map.
Facilitator Notes:
Focus on relative comparison rather than trying to score items perfectly.

Challenge assumptions about effort and impact.

Use discussion to resolve major disagreements but avoid over-analysing individual items.

The goal is to identify which opportunities should be pursued first.

Name: Priority Map
Purpose: Help teams compare options and agree what should be prioritised first.
Preparation Needed:
Prepare a prioritisation framework and agree the decision criteria before the session begins.

Ensure all options are visible and understood by participants.
Facilitator Notes:
Make the prioritisation criteria explicit before starting.

Challenge opinions that are not supported by evidence.

Focus on creating agreement around what should happen next rather than creating a perfect ranking.

Use voting techniques if the group becomes stuck.

Name: Start Stop Continue
Purpose: Reflect on current behaviours, processes or ways of working and identify what should start, stop or continue.
Outcomes: Action planning, Alignment, Shared understanding, Team alignment
Preparation Needed:
Prepare three areas labelled:

Start
Stop
Continue

Ensure participants understand the topic being reviewed before beginning the activity.
Facilitator Notes:
Focus on behaviours, processes and ways of working rather than individuals.

Encourage constructive feedback.

Look for recurring themes and patterns.

Finish by agreeing which actions will be taken forward.
